title: A larger body in a tidal field
hook: Change separation between points and predict leading tidal acceleration difference.
misconception: leading tidal acceleration difference stays fixed when separation between points doubles.
objective: Apply tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³ to compare leading tidal acceleration difference when separation between points changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a separation much shorter than fixed distance from a fixed point-mass source, tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³. When separation between points doubles, leading tidal acceleration difference becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a separation much shorter than fixed distance from a fixed point-mass source, with a nonzero initial result. If separation between points triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on leading tidal acceleration difference?
recall.why: Apply tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³ under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
